title: Peel the ring-pull lid off a light 85 g cat-food can, holding the can down so it neither lifts nor tips
instruction: Open the can of cat food: take its lid right off and put the lid down on the table away from the can, without spilling any food.
context: Anyone who feeds a cat or opens a tin of tuna does this: 49 million US households own a cat (APPA, 2025). The filled can weighs about 105 g, so pulling its ring takes several times its weight; held only by the ring it comes up with the lid or tips over and spills.
setup: On the table (standing in for a kitchen counter), positions in the robot frame (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left, arm bases at x 0, y +-30.5 cm): one unopened Purina Fancy Feast 85 g (3 oz) cat-food can, size 211 x 108 (6.8 cm across the top seam, 6.5 cm body, 3.8 cm tall), tinplate steel, 105 g filled, standing upright with its axis at x 30 cm, y +3 cm. Its full-aperture easy-open end: a 5.7 cm panel inside the score line, sitting 4.5 mm below the top of the seam; a steel ring-pull tab riveted 1.45 cm in from the score on the +y side (toward the left arm), its 2.0 cm-wide ring pointing at the panel's centre (-y) and formed slightly upward, its free end about 3 mm off the panel. Distractors, which scoring ignores (NVIDIA SimReady props): a red ceramic cat bowl, 16.3 cm across and 5.5 cm tall, 350 g, centred at x 52 cm, y +17 cm; a blue plastic spoon, 15.7 x 3.5 cm, 6 g, lying at x 20 cm, y +25 cm, turned 29 degrees; a blue plastic fork, 15.8 x 3.0 cm, 6 g, lying at x 53 cm, y -20 cm, turned -23 degrees.
scoring: 0.0 if at any moment the can tips more than 30 degrees from upright or its base rises more than 2 cm off the table (food spilled or dropped), whatever happens after; otherwise 0.0 if the score never pops. 0.25: the score has popped (the ring lifted 8 degrees on its rivet, about 4 mm at its end) but less than half the score line is torn. 0.5: at least half the score line is torn (simulator: the panel has been turned 90 degrees or more about the far side of its score). 0.75: the panel has come fully away from the can, but the full-credit conditions below are not all met. 1.0: the panel is off and lies on the table (its centre at most 12 mm above the tabletop) with its centre at least 9 cm from the can's axis; the can is upright within 5 degrees with its base within 3 mm of the table; every fingertip is at least 3 cm from the can and from the panel and its ring; the can and the panel each move less than 1 cm/s; all of this held together for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: The can is a consumable: each trial uses a new unopened can of the same product. The opened can and its lid go in the recycling (the lid's edge is sharp).
fidelity: Can, lid and ring tab are custom meshes at real size (no SimReady easy-open can); bowl, spoon and fork are SimReady. The lid is a rigid 4 g flap that turns about the far side of its score instead of curling. The pop is a sprung rivet joint that lets go at 8 degrees (about 15 N at the ring's end); the tear is a hand-set resistance that never springs back, with a last segment that breaks past 105 degrees. No food is simulated: tipping stands in for spilling. Uniform rubber-like friction.
scores: NOT VALIDATED: Dream-1 run: not run; demo: 0.0 so far (the scripted demo has not yet popped the score)
